content.overview: Article 226 is the High Court gateway for PIL; it may enforce fundamental rights and also other legal rights for any other purpose, subject to territorial limits and judicial self-restraint on standing.
content.study: PIL is a rule of standing, not a new writ. Article 226 is wider than Article 32 in the kinds of rights enforceable, but liberalised standing still requires bona fide public interest. Private disputes dressed as PIL fail. Prefer 226 for region-specific public wrongs and non-Part-III public duties; prefer 32 for Supreme Court Part III enforcement. Cross-read the constitutional Article 226 topic for territorial and writ-power detail.
